runs.content:
**Investigation idea:** The /options-trade-recommender skill's first run has no wiki output file — its actual recommendations exist only as a one-line log.md summary, invisible to the very idea page it analyzed. finance/michael-burry/burry-options-approach.md and finance/concepts/concept-options-trading.md were both created 2026-07-31 alongside the new skill, whose first run produced 5 concrete WDAY recommendations (top pick: a $150 Sep 19 covered call ahead of Aug 20 earnings IV crush, IV rank ~85-90%, per log.md). Unlike every other recommender skill in the wiki — book-recommender → books/suggestions.md, podcast-recommender → podcasts/suggestions.md, recipe-recommender → cooking's weekly suggestions page — options-trade-recommender wrote no output file at all: a wiki-wide search for the run's own figures (the Sep 19 expiry, the $150 strike) returns zero matches anywhere in wiki/. That data is now unrecoverable outside log.md's summary line. Worse, finance/ideas/idea-wday.md — the one page that should have received this analysis, since it's the same ticker — still carries only its own stale May 29 options section (cash-secured puts at $120, Strategies A/B/C from two months earlier) with no reference to the July 31 run at all. Next step: give options-trade-recommender an output-file convention (e.g. wiki/finance/options-suggestions.md, mirroring the other three recommenders), backfill this first run's 5 WDAY recommendations into it, and cross-link from idea-wday.md.

**Cross-domain connection:** Michael Burry's newest long thesis is explicitly a bet on regulated sportsbooks beating prediction markets — and Sports Betting's own bookmaker tracker is still an empty placeholder. finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-07-24.md and source-burry-trading-post-2026-07-30.md both show Burry building DraftKings (DKNG) into "a larger position" (paired with Flutter/FLUT, FanDuel's parent) — the July 30 page's own Interpretation Notes label it explicitly as an "anti-prediction-markets long thesis": a bet that regulated sportsbook incumbents outcompete or outlast the Kalshi/Polymarket-style prediction-market entrants encroaching on sports betting. sports-betting/markets.md's own "Bookmakers on Radar" table has been a single "[to be added]" placeholder row since 2026-05-01, and sports-betting/overview.md's "Key Questions to Answer" doesn't ask about bookmaker-vs-prediction-market competitive dynamics at all — despite this being live, current market-structure information about the exact industry the domain is trying to find edge in. Neither Burry source page nor either Sports Betting page cites the other. Next step: add DraftKings/Flutter to markets.md's Bookmakers table, and note the prediction-markets competitive threat as a dynamic worth tracking alongside CLV/model-edge work.

**Resolved:** book-gladiator.md was created 2026-08-01 but missing from wiki/index.md's Books table (originally logged 2026-08-01) — confirmed today: index.md now carries the book-gladiator row alongside book-bad-actors. Not fully closed — the page's own title-verification flag (no confirmed Con Iggulden novel titled Gladiator in his bibliography) remains open, still paired with the pre-existing book-even-the-darkest-night flag.

Sunday focus (whichever domain has gone longest without a deep-dive): chose Work — the most stagnant domain (2 pages, unchanged since 2026-05-15) — and deep-read work/overview.md, work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026.md, and finance/ideas/idea-wday.md. Found the domain itself already exhaustively cross-linked from prior runs, so both findings this run came from checking Finance's most recent activity (the July 31 options-trade-recommender run, Burry's July 24/30 trading posts) against pages that hadn't been checked against it yet. log.md since the last thinker run (2026-08-01) showed no other new wiki activity beyond a routine spinoff-monitor update already reflected in memory/index.md's Open Threads.

**Investigation idea:** Today's book-summarizer run added Bad Actors to index.md but not Gladiator — and Gladiator's own page carries an unresolved title-verification flag identical to book-even-the-darkest-night's already-flagged issue. books/book-gladiator.md and books/book-bad-actors.md were both created today (2026-08-01) by the monthly book-summarizer, resolving the 2026-07-16 open idea about Gladiator sitting unprocessed for a month — but wiki/index.md's Books table was updated with the Bad Actors row and not the Gladiator row, leaving the newest addition invisible to the master catalog exactly the way the old idea warned it would be if nobody intervened. Separately, book-gladiator.md's own "Note on verification" section flags that no standalone Conn Iggulden novel titled Gladiator could be confirmed in his published bibliography (closest candidates: The Gates of Rome / The Death of Kings from the Emperor series, or a possible mix-up with Simon Scarrow's YA Gladiator series) — closely mirroring the unresolved [uncertain] flag already sitting on books/book-even-the-darkest-night.md. Two separate reading-list entries now carry the same class of unverified bibliographic detail, six weeks apart, with no process fix in between. Next step: add the missing index.md row for book-gladiator, and raise both open verification flags with Fred in the same pass.

**Cross-domain connection:** Technology's own Ukraine defence-manufacturing source page is a live, dated proof point for exactly the NATO capability gap Finance's Rheinmetall bull case cites in the abstract — and neither page mentions the other. finance/ideas/idea-rheinmetall.md's bull case rests on "NATO capability gaps identified by the Ukraine conflict" — ammunition, air defense, armored vehicles — as the structural demand driver behind Germany's largest defense-spending increase in decades. technology/source-guardian-fire-point-ukraine-missiles-2026-07-27.md documents the demand side of that exact gap concretely: Fire Point, Ukraine's own indigenous deep-strike manufacturer, scaling from 18 to 6,000 employees and producing ~100 Flamingo cruise missiles/month plus hundreds of drones/day, alongside a new "Freyja" Patriot-alternative air-defence initiative — the same ammunition/air-defense categories Rheinmetall's own bull case names as its core exposure. idea-rheinmetall.md was last updated 2026-06-13, three weeks before the Fire Point clipping existed, so the omission is a timing gap rather than an oversight — but it's now a ready, concrete real-world data point bearing on the thesis either way: evidence of the scale/urgency of the capability gap, or an open question of whether growing Ukrainian domestic production is a long-term tailwind or a substitution risk to European primes like Rheinmetall. Next step: add a line to idea-rheinmetall.md's bull case citing Fire Point, with a note on which side of that question it falls.

Saturday focus (full sweep — skim every domain's overview/index page rather than deep-reading one, bias toward connections): reviewed memory/index.md, wiki/index.md, and log.md since the last thinker run (2026-07-31); today's only new wiki activity was book-summarizer (Gladiator, Bad Actors) and spinoff-monitor (Delivery Hero, Valmet, Bayer/BP/Voya/Disney status updates — Delivery Hero and Bayer already carry their own explicit next-step notes within concept-spinoff-investing.md, so not duplicated here). Skimmed Games, Sports Betting, Crypto, Work, and Cooking overview pages (all unchanged since 2026-05-01) plus Finance's Rheinmetall and spinoff pages; the Rheinmetall/Fire Point connection surfaced from cross-checking a June Finance idea page against a late-July Technology clipping that postdated it.
